facts.fact: Access Now says that after the 2021 block the regulator ZICTA entered a consent judgment undertaking not to act outside its authority to interrupt internet access and to give the reason for any future interruption within 36 hours; the letter urges the government to honour it. The document gives no date for the judgment, so its published date is used as when the undertaking stood.

facts.fact: Access to major social media platforms such as Facebook, Twitter and Instagram was cut off in Zambia on election day, 12 August 2021, and the following day; the government said it could not establish the cause.

note: The 2026 coalition letter is a call to keep the internet on, not criticism of a named policy; the cut is the 2021 one the letter recalls.

facts.fact: The Net Rights Coalition, whose members include Bloggers of Zambia, Common Cause Zambia and the Zambia Free Press Initiative, said in a statement that arrests, detention and summoning of journalists under the Cyber Crimes Act No. 4 of 2025 signal a chilling environment for the media, and called for amendments to the cyber laws.
The coalition recalled that Zambia's internet shutdown of August 2021, coinciding with the presidential election, affected access to social media platforms.

note: Arrests of journalists under the Cyber Crimes Act are mentioned but the document gives no names, dates or what they said, so no punished fact.

Ndola TikToker arrested on 2026-09-19 for allegedly harassing truck drivers on a private association's complaint; the speech is about truck drivers, not the government, an official or public affairs, and the charge is behind the paywall: no fact.

facts.fact: The Lusaka Magistrates Court sentenced vlogger Joseph Chishimba to nine months for posting in a WhatsApp group in October 2024 a screenshot claiming a presidential aide, Chipo Mwanawasa, was made pregnant by a man at State House, under section 54 (publication of information) of the Cyber Security and Cyber Crimes Act No. 2 of 2021.

Police in Mansa arrested Kennedy Mwansa, 38, for allegedly insulting President Hakainde Hichilema in a TikTok video, charging him under the Cyber Crimes Act with harassment using electronic gadgets; the arrest date is not given, the police statement was on Friday 2026-09-11 and the video was reported to police on 2026-09-09, so the statement date is used.
